messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: prod-west-03 GPU pool 96% util, queue depth ~3.8k, enqueue 429/503 spike. Auto-opened INC-4001 and notified #incidents
lily: ack — oncall-sre here. pulling autoscaler + operator logs. @arjun @maya please join. :eyes:
arjun: infra ack. checking cloud quota and node provisioning. initial glance: scale attempts rejected by pool hard cap and reconciler panic observed. grabbing full logs.
maya: ml oncall ack. checking recent rollouts — there was a canary for embed-slim yesterday that increased per-request memory ~1.8x. also noticing an external synthetic load test hitting the same endpoints starting ~11:05. might be compounding.
kevin: infra operator logs snippet:
```
E0315 11:07:24 autoscaler.go:410] ScaleRejected: PoolHardLimit pool=prod-west-03 cap=260 requested=30
E0315 11:07:24 reconcile.go:316] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer deref
W0315 11:08:24 autoscaler.go:428] backoff next attempt in 120s (failures=6)
```
nate: support — customers reporting elevated latency and intermittent 429s. small set of realtime enterprise customers impacted. CS is triaging and prepping an interim message.
ops-bot: [action] incident created INC-4001 by incident-bot
lily: immediate mitigation plan (fast-parallel):
1) restart operator, apply nil-guard hotfix (fast)
2) request emergency manual scale +24 GPUs (parallel to 1)
3) divert ~40% of canary/opt traffic to stable model + enable cached fallback for low-priority routes
4) open cloud-support for quota bump and track provisioning
arjun: restarting operator and applying nil-guard now. will trigger reconcile after healthy.
ops-bot: [action] operator_restart id=op-6167-01
arjun: hotfix pr #4950 applied to guard nils in reconcile loop:
```
- if token.Len() == 0 {
+ if obj == nil || obj.token == nil || obj.token.Len() == 0 {
    return errors.New("invalid token")
 }
```
arjun: requesting emergency quota bump from cloud now.
cloud-support: temporary quota bump approved: +40 GPUs for 1 hour (request cs-7782). provisioning nodes — ETA ~12-25 minutes.
kevin: manual_scale submitted id=ms-616700-01 — provisioning started. note: autoscaler backoff windows prevent immediate retry; I'll force a reconcile trigger after operator healthy.
lily: applied traffic-split: embed-slim -> 40% reroute to embed-stable; enabled cache-fallback for /v1/realtime non-critical routes. ingress metrics show queue slope flattening.
nate: interim customer comms posted: "We're investigating a capacity issue affecting realtime inference in prod-west. Mitigations are underway; improvements expected within 15-25 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and next steps." :memo:
maya: looking at request traces — the synthetic load test was using an internal test key that wasn't whitelisted; it's generating high QPS and high memory per-request. adding isolation for load-test keys to action items.
kevin: post-recovery logs:
```
I0315 11:12:47 reconcile.go:120] reconcile success: pool=prod-west-03 scaled +24 -> available nodes 268
I0315 11:13:02 autoscaler.go:220] queue_depth=3800 -> 1200 after traffic split and scale
```
lily: status update: mitigated -> stabilizing. peak queue ~3.9k, now ~900 and steadily dropping. 429/503 rates back toward baseline. monitoring for 45 minutes.
olivia: product note: require a resource-impact assessment for rollouts that increase per-request memory >1.2x. owner: olivia. due in 10 days.
arjun: infra action items (owners/due):
- make reconcile backoff smarter: treat PoolHardLimit rejections differently so backoff isn't overly aggressive (owner: arjun, due: 3d)
- add failover rule to reroute traffic to other regions when queue >2k and scale requests failing (owner: arjun, due: 3d)
- add detection for synthetic load test keys and isolate test traffic (owner: arjun, due: 2d)
maya: ml action: cap per-rollout memory delta and add preflight synthetic workload run for resource-impacting changes (owner: maya, due: 7d)
nate: support action: finalize customer incident message and coordinate follow-ups (owner: nate, due: 1d)
lily: creating postmortem doc INC-4001 in tracker and scheduling review. postmortem link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4001
ops-bot: incident thread closed into doc INC-4001 at 6167000185
lily: final summary: root cause = combination of (1) canary increased per-request memory, (2) unexpected synthetic load using shared key, and (3) operator crashloop causing autoscaler backoff. mitigations applied: operator hotfix, manual scale, traffic split, cache fallback, quota bump. next steps above.
